title: Calibration does not certify its independence premises
statement: Shared channel error can make all contrasts and agreement look perfect while every aligned vote repeats one noisy bit. Codeword-correlated bootstrap noise can preserve all short checks without independent repair evidence. Input-dependent errors can give high average pair agreement while hard input regions retain large majority error;conditional independence given Xalone is insufficient. Unpaired examples with exact masks remain ordinary passive noisy-parity examples;any hardness conclusion additionally needs its LPN assumption and does not apply to the paired positive experiment. A common approximate anchor corruption can propagate to every corrected target. A failed sufficient confidence gate is not an information limit;other learners may succeed.
